[LADP.8.5.2] **A kwarg's declared type decides the number the service
receives.** A service sees a plain number, so the declaration is the contract.
The compiler must lower a quantity supplied by a kwarg's `default`
([LADP.8.5.1]), and a quantity written at the `call` on a kwarg whose declared
type is not a unit symbol, as follows:

| Declared type | The service receives |
|---|---|
| a unit symbol | the quantity expressed in that unit |
| a dimension or scalar-group name ([LUNI.7.1]) | the quantity in the dimension's base unit |
| `Float` or `Int` | the quantity in its dimension's base unit and storage type ([LUNI.7.2]) |

The compiler must reject a written quantity whose dimension is not the
kwarg's, on a unit-typed or dimension-typed kwarg (`DS_VALIDATE_DIM_MISMATCH`,
[LUNI.8.2]), unless exactly one `implicit` formula bridges the two dimensions,
which the compiler then applies ([LUNI.4.5.1]). A `default` of another
dimension is refused at the declaration ([LGRA.23.2]).

A written number with no unit, on a unit-typed or dimension-typed kwarg, is
taken as already in the kwarg's unit, or in the base unit for a dimension, as a
`let` annotation takes one ([LUNI.8.6]). The service receives it unchanged.
